dualGuide.title: Dual Editor (1-to-1 Comparison)
dualGuide.subtitle: Ideal for checking two specific files side-by-side.
dualGuide.step1: Select the programming language from the top toolbar.
dualGuide.step2: Upload a file or paste your code directly into the left and right editors.
dualGuide.step3: Click the "Analyze" button to run the comparison.
dualGuide.step4: Check the "Overall Similarity" score at the bottom. Click the "View Differences" icon to see highlighted matches.

bulkGuide.title: Bulk Editor (Multiple Files)
bulkGuide.subtitle: Analyze entire classrooms or project folders at once.
bulkGuide.step1: Select the programming language from the top toolbar.
bulkGuide.step2: Set your desired Similarity Threshold percentage. Only files matching above this limit will be grouped.
bulkGuide.step3: Upload multiple source files or a single ZIP archive containing your code.
bulkGuide.step4: Select files in the file manager to include in the analysis.
bulkGuide.step5: Click "Analyze" to process all selected files simultaneously.
bulkGuide.step6: Review the generated Similarity Groups. Expand a group to view diffs or inspect individual files.

q1.a: Currently, we support Python, Java, and C++. We are actively working on adding more languages in the near future.

q2.q: Can I paste code directly instead of uploading files?
q2.a: Yes! You can paste code directly into the provided text editors for both files in the "Dual Editor" section. Just make sure to select the correct programming language before analyzing.

q3.q: How does the Similarity Threshold work?
q3.a: The threshold is a percentage value (0% to 100%) that determines how strict the grouping algorithm should be. For example, setting it to 50% means the tool will flag and group files that share at least half of their logical structure. You can adjust this slider in the Bulk Editor before running the analysis.

q4.q: Is there a limit to the number of files for the "Bulk Editor"?
q4.a: You can upload individual files or compress them into a ZIP archive for easier uploading. Currently, there is a limit of 50 files per bulk analysis to ensure optimal performance.

q5.a: That cap only applies to this hosted instance, to keep it responsive on Render's free tier. If you run CSIM Online locally, you can change or remove it by editing the MAX_FILES_IN_BULK_EDITOR constant in ui/src/utils/table.js. See the "Run Locally" quick link above for setup instructions.

q1.q: What does the overall similarity percentage mean?
q1.a: The similarity percentage indicates how much of the logical code structure in the files is identical. A 100% match means the logic is identical, while lower percentages indicate partial reuse. Use the "View Differences" (diff) button in the results to see the exact matching lines highlighted.

q1.q: How do I use the Action Buttons in the results?
q1.a: Hover over any button in the app to see a descriptive tooltip. In the results panel, you will find buttons to expand file groups, view side-by-side differences (Diff Viewer), or inspect the raw file content.

q2.a: Yes, the download and export features are available in the top right corner of the results panel. Currently, this is only available in the "Bulk Editor" section.

q1.q: How accurate is the plagiarism detection?
q1.a: Our algorithm compares deep code structure and logic, not just plain text. For best results, analyze complete files rather than short snippets. The accuracy improves with larger code samples.

q2.q: Should I analyze compiled or source code?
q2.a: Always use raw source code files (.py, .cpp, .java). Compiled code or executables cannot be analyzed.

q3.q: Can the tool detect obfuscated code?
q3.a: Because our tool analyzes logical structure and variable usage patterns rather than just text matching, it can bypass basic obfuscation like renaming variables or changing indentation.
